key_insight: Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ shows magnetoresistive memory, where resistivity depends on both magnetic-field strength and its history, and this occurs unusually in the paramagnetic phase above the antiferromagnetic transition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new route to nonvolatile sensing and memory devices based on correlated-electron materials that can retain field history without magnetic order.
method: Measure resistivity versus magnetic-field history and magnitude
Map temperature dependence across the antiferromagnetic transition
Analyze time-dependent response to distinguish memory from simple magnetoresistance
evidence_signal: The abstract reports field-, temperature-, and time-dependent resistivity behavior that reveals memory onset at about twice the antiferromagnetic transition temperature.
watch_item: The mechanism is not yet identified, so hidden order or short-range correlations must be verified before device implementation.
paper_title: Magnetoresistive Memory in the Paramagnetic Phase of Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$
